figures.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram / editorial illustration edit.
Asset type: a detailed companion illustration in a serious business book.
Input: the provided image is the earlier illustration to expand; use its warm ivory paper, hand-inked dark navy outlines, muted teal and ochre palette, restrained texture, simple contemporary clothing and diverse adult characters as the visual style reference.
Primary request: RECOMPOSE the earlier three-stage landscape diagram into a PORTRAIT 3:4 illustration, ideally 1536 by 2048 pixels, with SIX equally sized illustrated panels in exactly TWO COLUMNS and THREE ROWS. The new illustration must cover every row of a table about investment's effects on working relationships.
Layout: six neatly aligned panels with generous ivory gutters and thin navy separator lines. Read left to right, top to bottom. Each panel has a bold dark navy uppercase heading at the top, one specific readable scene in the middle, and its exact short explanatory caption at the bottom. Headings must be very large and captions large enough for article reading, with clean line breaks. The longer heading CAPABILITY & CONFIDENCE may wrap over two lines. Safe margins on all sides. Render all six panels completely; crop nothing. No overall title, no legend, no decorative outer frame. The six qualities are parallel dimensions, NOT six steps: do NOT put connecting arrows between panels, and remove the old long return arrow.
All six required headings, in order: TRUST; OPEN DISAGREEMENT; COMMITMENT; ACCOUNTABILITY; CAPABILITY & CONFIDENCE; SHARED PURPOSE.
Keep scenes concrete and explanatory, with two or three people and only the props needed to show the mechanism. These are ordinary work interactions, not villains, caricatures, dramatic disasters or stock-photo dashboards. No charts, numbers, pseudo-text, tiny annotations, slogans, watermark or signature. Use only the exact headings and short captions given below; where indicated a speech bubble may contain the additional specified words. Diagrams on papers should use simple symbols and lines. Both illustrations in the pair must use the same six-panel arrangement and typographic hierarchy.

This is the CONSTRUCTIVE version. Teal is the main accent, with restrained ochre details. People are attentive and cooperative, not jubilant.
Panel 1 TRUST. Scene: an investor representative and company leader openly examine a funding plan with a calendar, a modest stack of coins and a prominent checked condition. Both can see the same information; a small corrected line with a tick suggests an acknowledged mistake. Caption exactly: "Conditions clear. Promises kept."
Panel 2 OPEN DISAGREEMENT. Scene: one team member points to a question on a plan; a leader and colleague listen at the same table and examine two alternative cards. One speech bubble contains only a large question mark. Caption exactly: "Questions welcome before decisions."
Panel 3 COMMITMENT. Scene: two colleagues choose a SMALL number of work cards that fit inside a clearly bounded tray beside available resource tokens; additional cards are deliberately set aside in a separate waiting pile. A simple calendar accompanies the chosen work. Caption exactly: "Priorities fit the resources."
Panel 4 ACCOUNTABILITY. Scene: a leader and team member each hold their own task card with a paired decision stamp and check box. They review progress together on one shared board with TWO matching responsibility lanes, making clear that responsibility and authority belong together for both parties. Caption exactly: "Authority and responsibility match."
Panel 5 CAPABILITY & CONFIDENCE. Scene: a visiting specialist works SIDE BY SIDE with a company colleague to repair a recurring problem in a simple gear mechanism. Both practise with tools and share one open method notebook. The company colleague operates the now-working mechanism, showing learning retained inside the team. Caption exactly: "Support leaves people more capable."
Panel 6 SHARED PURPOSE. Scene: four people representing an investor, company leader, employee and customer sit around one shared plan. Four distinct simple interest symbols (coin, gear, team, customer) feed into a central agreed-outcome card; no interest is obscured or erased. Caption exactly: "Different interests. Agreed outcomes."
Do not retain the old three-stage headings or the TRUST GROWS return arrow. Include all six named dimensions once each.

figures.caption: Investment can build trust and cooperation through clear conditions, open discussion, realistic commitments, accountable decisions, shared learning and agreed outcomes.
figures.visual_review: All six labelled panels and explanatory captions inspected. Scenes show clear conditions, welcome questions, bounded priorities, matched authority and responsibility, retained learning and openly agreed outcomes. Table order and shared palette are correct.
